### Observed differences

- In the later window, A32 and A33 run in about 55 in 100 cases (109 of 200 traces each, against 1 and 0 of 200 before). They always appear together in the same traces, in either order — A32 before A33 in about 21 in 100 cases, A33 before A32 in about 34 in 100 — and around the middle of the trace (median relative position about 0.5). [OCC005, OCC006, REL016, POS002, POS003]
- Routing into this pair is visible at A26: before, about 98 in 100 of A26's outgoing transitions went to A27; in the later window about 44 in 100 go to A27, about 33 to A33 and about 20 to A32. The new activities hand over to each other and to A28 (from A32: about 61 in 100 transitions to A28 and 39 to A33; from A33: about 61 to A32 and 38 to A28). [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- The former A26 → A27 → A28 segment still runs but less often: A27 now appears in about 45 in 100 traces (91 of 200, against all 200 before), while A28 still appears in every trace; where A27 runs it still precedes A28, and A26 still precedes A27. [OCC004, REL006, REL009, REL014]
- Order and distance evidence matches one extra step on the path: A26 precedes A32 and A33, and A32/A33 precede A28, each in the same ~55 in 100 traces; the distance from A26 to A28 moved from 2 steps (about 99 in 100 cases before) to 3 steps (about 54 in 100 after). [REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, LAG002]
- In the later window A04 appears in about 11 in 100 traces, down from about 29 in 100; its outgoing transitions shifted from about 88 in 100 going to A44 to a spread (A44 about 23, A46 about 18, A16 about 14 in 100), and A43 now sends about 92 in 100 of its transitions to A44 (about 68 before) and almost none to A04 (about 3 vs 30 in 100). A04 also appears earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.83 to 0.61). [OCC001, DIR001, DIR005, POS001]
- Participation also shifted elsewhere: A23 from about 59 to 41 in 100 traces, A24 from about 42 to 60 in 100. [OCC002, OCC003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, a block of A32 and A33 — always executed together, in either order — sits between A26 and A28 in about 55 in 100 cases, while the previous A26 → A27 → A28 segment continues in the remaining cases with A27 at about half its former participation. The rerouting is observed directly at A26 and at the new activities' outgoing edges, and the ordering relations (A26 before A32/A33, A32/A33 before A28) hold in exactly the share of traces in which the new activities run. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, OCC004]

The account is consistent across occurrence, routing, positional and relational indicators, though several of them describe the same traces and are not independent confirmations; the one-step increase in the A26→A28 distance (2 to 3) matches exactly one extra activity on the path. With 38 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected if nothing had changed, and shifts of the size of A33 going from 0 to 109 traces and A26→A27 from about 98 to 44 in 100 transitions, sampling variation cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [LAG002, OCC006, DIR002]

Limitations: the evidence does not establish whether the A04 and A43 changes belong to the same structural difference — A04's destination mix in the later window rests on only about 22 outgoing transitions, and the A23/A24 participation shifts have no relational evidence behind them, so variant-frequency sampling between the two windows remains a plausible explanation for these smaller differences. A33's absence before only means it was not observed in that window, although with 200 traces per window its later presence in 109 is unlikely to be a sampling artefact. [DIR001, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC006]
